_comment_family: Montserrat ships as a family of static cuts, and the three in this
folder are named by that family inconsistently - which is the whole
reason all three packs declare a full name instead of a family.
This file's name ID 1 is 'Montserrat', flat, with 'Bold' as its
subfamily: the Bold is one of the four styles the old family model
allows, so it answers to the family name itself. Its SemiBold and
ExtraBold neighbours cannot, and each carries its own full name as
name ID 1. Asking for 'Montserrat' here would therefore be asking for
a name the Bold shares with every other cut of Montserrat a machine
happens to have installed - the Regular among them - and the channels
set in these faces would be blocks silently set in whichever weight
So the full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, the same way
telegraf-ultralight and raleway-bold declare theirs. Three files,
three distinct family names, which is also what lets one channel be
set in two of them at once (see `highlight.face` in js/channels.js):
fontguard keys its check by family, so each cut is verified in its
own right rather than one check answering for the rest.
_comment_weight: 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. It matters more here than it usually would, because this cut
sits in the middle of the three and is a step away from both of them:
it is the block expulsion-science picks words out of in the 800, and
it is the highlight rap-lore picks words with out of the 600. Either
way the difference between two cuts IS the channel's highlight, and a
block asked for at the wrong weight would not look wrong on its own -
it would quietly close the one gap the highlight is made of.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4) and the second the
PostScript name; both name this one cut rather than the family, so a
machine answering to either is answering with the Bold.
'Montserrat' on its own is deliberately absent, for the reason given
above: it is this file's own name ID 1, and it is also the name every
other weight of Montserrat installed on the machine answers to. It is
the one entry that could hand back a Regular - which on rap-lore,
where this cut is the highlight, would be a picked word lighter than
the words either side of it.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied.
No Impact and no Arial Black, which most of this folder falls through
and which would be wrong twice over. Montserrat is a geometric text
sans at 700, not a heavy display cut, so a condensed grotesque behind
it is the furthest thing the machine could offer from what went
missing. And the Montserrat packs are weight pairs: dropping either
half of a pair into a face with one weight would take the highlight
with it.
Segoe UI is on every Windows this app runs on and has a real Bold;
Arial is the floor and has one too. All three packs share these
entries and differ only in the weight they reach them at - 600, 700
and 800 - so the weight step survives a missing file as far as the
substitute family has the weights to survive it. Neither substitute
has a SemiBold, so the 600 lands on a Regular or a Bold depending on
the machine, and where it lands on the Bold the picked words come out
set as their neighbours.
That is the ordinary cost of a face that never arrived, and it is
reported rather than drawn.
